scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: super_spine_router_0 zebra
Mechanism: zebra is FRR's RIB/kernel-interface daemon. It was killed
  together with watchfrr (its watchdog), so nothing respawns it, while
  bgpd keeps running: the BGP sessions to spine_router_0_0
  (172.16.0.1) and spine_router_0_1 (172.16.0.3) stay Established
  because bgpd owns its own TCP sessions. The failure is in the
  management/route-programming plane: zebra-owned CLI queries (route
  table, interface state) fail, and bgpd can no longer program new
  routes into the kernel. Forwarding continues on the kernel FIB that
  zebra had already installed (a SIGKILL leaves kernel routes in
  place), and in this size-s fabric the super-spine is not even on the
  pc_0_0 <-> pc_0_1 data path (that path is leaf -> spine -> leaf), so
  there is no user impact -- but the device would blackhole any future
  route change it needs zebra to program.
Localization: super_spine_router_0
Root cause: zebra not running on super_spine_router_0 (bgpd still up)
Fix: restart FRR on super_spine_router_0 (`service frr restart`) --
  the config persists in /etc/frr/frr.conf, so the restart brings back
  zebra, watchfrr and bgpd cleanly.

Observable note: the kill uses the same watchfrr-first pattern as the
lab-verified bgpd kills on this fabric (nothing respawns the daemon).
With zebra dead but bgpd alive, `pgrep zebra` is empty while
`pgrep bgpd` still returns a process; zebra-owned vtysh queries (e.g.
the route table) error out while BGP state remains queryable from the
peers. An agent that describes this as "FRR is partially down /
zebra crashed on super_spine_router_0" has found the fault.
scenario.fix_spec:
`service frr restart` on super_spine_router_0. The persistent
/etc/frr/frr.conf restores zebra (and watchfrr) alongside bgpd; the
route-programming and CLI/telemetry plane recovers, and the BGP
sessions re-establish.

agent.diagnosis_text:
**Affected component:** The FRR routing-daemon stack on `super_spine_router_0` — specifically the `zebra` routing-information-base (RIB) manager and the `watchfrr` process watchdog. Only `bgpd` (PID 57) is running on that device.

**Mechanism:** `zebra` is the FRR core daemon that owns the kernel routing table and exposes interface state to the FRR CLI via a Unix socket. When `vtysh` (or any audit tool) issues route-table or interface queries, it connects to `zebra`'s socket; with `zebra` absent, every such call returns a "daemon-connection error". `bgpd` is architecturally independent of `zebra` for its TCP peering sessions — the BGP hold-timer keepalives continue to flow over the existing TCP connections to `spine_router_0_0` and `spine_router_0_1`, so both spines still report those sessions as Established. The kernel routing table on `super_spine_router_0` retains whatever routes were installed before `zebra` stopped, so forwarding for `pc_0_0 ↔ pc_0_1` traffic continues uninterrupted. The absence of `watchfrr` means the FRR watchdog that would detect and auto-restart `zebra` is also gone, so the failure is persistent until manually corrected.

**Localization:** `super_spine_router_0` only — all four other FRR routers show `watchfrr=yes`, `zebra=yes`, `bgpd=yes` and have no command errors.

**Root cause:** The `zebra` and `watchfrr` daemons on `super_spine_router_0` are not running (only `bgpd` is active), leaving the FRR CLI unable to service any routing-table or interface-state queries.

**Fix:** Run `systemctl restart frr` on `super_spine_router_0` to bring `zebra` and `watchfrr` back up alongside `bgpd`.

per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly localizes the fault to super_spine_router_0 (states affected component and localization as that device).

Restarting the FRR service on super_spine_router_0 will bring zebra and watchfrr back up, restoring route programming and the CLI/telemetry plane so BGP sessions and routing recover.
